summary: Defines three Elliptic Curve Cryptography groups based on modular arithmetic modulo a prime, for use in IKE and IKEv2. They align the protocols with NIST standards and can be more efficient than earlier ECC groups. It is informational and replaced RFC 4753.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds three elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman groups for IKE and IKEv2. It also specifies how peers encode public curve points and which part of their shared result becomes the secret.

subtitle: Three prime-field elliptic-curve groups and their key formats for IKE and IKEv2.

tldr.problem: IKE and IKEv2 needed additional elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman groups using prime-field arithmetic and aligned with other standards.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines groups with 256-bit, 384-bit and 521-bit fields and specifies the point coordinates and shared-secret format carried in key exchange.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5903 is Informational, replaces RFC 4753 and clarifies that the shared secret is the x coordinate of the common point.

facts.label: Shared secret
facts.value: x coordinate of the common point

today: RFC 5903 is an Informational RFC that obsoletes RFC 4753. It replaces the earlier shared-secret format with the x-coordinate rule.

sections.title: Why Add Prime-Field Groups
sections.content:
IKE and IKEv2 use Diffie-Hellman exchanges to establish shared secrets. RFC 5903 adds three elliptic-curve groups whose arithmetic is modulo a prime, in addition to previously defined groups.

The RFC says these groups can improve software efficiency and align IKE and IKEv2 with groups standardized by NIST, SECG, ISO and ANSI. It also says their security levels correspond to symmetric key sizes of 128, 192 and 256 bits.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC adds three curve groups for creating shared secrets in IKE and IKEv2. They use arithmetic modulo a prime and are also named in other standards.

sections.title: The Three ECP Groups
sections.content:
All three groups use the curve equation y^2 = x^3 - 3x + b over integers modulo a prime. Their field sizes are 256, 384 and 521 bits. The RFC gives each group's prime, curve constant, order and generator point.

Implementations of IKE and IKEv2 SHOULD support each group. The groups were chosen verifiably at random using SHA-1 as specified in IEEE 1363 and a published seed.
sections.plainLanguage: Each group has a specified prime, curve and starting point. The RFC gives those values so implementations can perform the same exchange.

sections.title: Public Values and the Shared Secret
sections.content:
An ECP public value contains the x and y coordinates of a curve point, concatenated in a Key Exchange (KE) payload. Each coordinate has a fixed length: 256 bits for the 256-bit group, 384 bits for the 384-bit group and 528 bits for the 521-bit group. Implementations prepend zeros when needed to reach that length.

The Diffie-Hellman shared secret is the x coordinate of the common point. The RFC says these encoding rules are specific to prime-field ECP curves and may not apply to binary-field EC2N curves.
sections.plainLanguage: Peers send both coordinates of their public curve points, using fixed lengths for each group. They use only the x coordinate of their common point as the shared secret.

sections.title: Correction to RFC 4753
sections.content:
RFC 4753 had said that the shared secret used the same format as the public value. RFC 5903 replaces that rule with the x coordinate of the Diffie-Hellman common value. The corrected format had appeared earlier in an erratum to RFC 4753.

Implementations that followed the erratum interoperate with this specification. Implementations that did not may calculate a different secret while using the same group code point, so peers may fail to communicate and the initiator may time out. The test vectors were updated to use the corrected format.
sections.plainLanguage: The new rule defines the shared secret as one coordinate, not the full public point. Peers using different rules for the same group may fail to establish a key.

sections.title: Security, Names and Group Identifiers
sections.content:
The RFC notes that security considerations from the IKE and IKEv2 specifications also apply to these groups. Each group corresponds to a symmetric key size of 128, 192 or 256 bits, respectively.

IANA added the groups to the IKE and IKEv2 Diffie-Hellman registries. Their identifiers are 19 for the 256-bit group, 20 for the 384-bit group and 21 for the 521-bit group. The RFC also lists their names in other standards, including P-256, P-384 and P-521.
sections.plainLanguage: The three groups were added to both IKE registries with identifiers 19, 20 and 21. Existing IKE and IKEv2 security guidance still applies.
